$comment: Code generated by scripts/generate-contracts.mjs from contracts/ (JSON Schema bundle); DO NOT EDIT.

archived.description: Native scanner state, independent of a Foundry-owned session.

transcriptBefore.description: `transcriptBefore` is the byte offset in the native log where Transcript starts when it holds only the log's latest part.

ChatArchive.description: Archive state is separate from execution status and never deletes history.

NativeArchiveItem.description: NativeArchiveItem is the minimal device request; persistence/results also retain observations and errors in NativeArchiveTarget.

NativeArchiveTarget.description: A native session's archive request and what its device last reported doing with it.

TranscriptMessage.description: Display records retain native semantics independently of handoff prose.

requestUsage.description: `requestUsage` is the tokens of the model request that produced this step (Claude).

turnUsage.description: `turnUsage`, on the answer that ended a turn, is the turn's usage read from the agent's own log (imported chats).

questions.description: `questions` an answer asks the person: without waiting (Codex request_user_input_async; Delivery is then "async"), holding the turn until answered or timed out (Claude AskUserQuestion), or ending the turn to wait for the answer as the next message (Delivery "next_turn": questions of a child session, relayed to its parent).

delivery.description: "async" on a message whose questions do not hold the turn; "next_turn" on one whose questions ended the turn and wait for the next message to answer them.

compaction.description: `compaction`, on a boundary, is the context compaction it marks (DEV-083).

AgentQuestion.description: AgentQuestion is one question an Agent asked; without options it takes free text only.

header.description: A short label of the question (Claude's chip, at most 12 characters).

options.description: Suggested answers; the recommended one first unless `unranked`. The answer to a chosen option is its text, verbatim.

descriptions.description: What choosing each option means, by option index (Claude).

multiSelect.description: Several options may be chosen; the answer joins them with ", " (Claude).

unranked.description: The order of the options recommends none (Claude, which names a recommendation in the option's own text).

approval.description: A permission prompt (Claude's ExitPlanMode or another tool needing approval), not a question; its options are "Approve" and "Deny", and any other answer denies with that answer as the reason.

detail.description: Markdown the question is about, shown above its choices (the plan an approval asks for).

ModelRequestUsage.description: ModelRequestUsage is one model request's tokens; steps of one request share its id and its last report counts.

inputTokens.description: Prompt tokens, cache reads and writes included.

ConnectorRequirement.description: ConnectorRequirement is a condition a device must meet for the connector to work there ("tcp_reachable": host:port opens within a few seconds).

label.description: What the requirement means to a person ("Company network").

ConnectorTool.description: ConnectorTool is the program a connector's sessions use and where Foundry installs it from ("npm" through the managed-tools path, "installer" through the vendor's official per-user installer, which the worker's adapter runs). MinimumVersion marks older copies as outdated.

source.description: "device": installed outside Foundry; "npm": a managed package; "installer": the vendor's official per-user installer, run by the worker's adapter at the owner's click.

registry.description: Where the package comes from; "device" is the device's own npm settings.

minimumVersion.description: Older copies work worse or not at all ("2.0.0" for AWS CLI v2).

ConnectorAuthorizationGroup.description: A shared credential requirement; multiple business capabilities can use it.

scopeSource.description: Where the scope list comes from; "All" is offered only when it is complete.

scopesRemovable.description: Unchecking a granted scope removes it (the tool can drop scopes); otherwise authorizing only adds.

required.description: Always requested and never removed (a tool's own minimum).

impliedBy.description: Broader scopes that include this one; granted when any of them is.

ConnectorScopeSource.description: The list a set of scopes was taken from.

url.description: An https page or listing endpoint.

complete.description: The source is the vendor's authoritative list of every scope (official docs, SDK or CLI constant, or a listing API).

source.description: foundry: an authorization or sign-in Foundry ran; outside: the tool's own login changed without Foundry (a terminal, another app, or a session that bypassed it).

at.description: When the device first read the changed set.

ConnectorPermissions.description: A connector whose permissions are not chosen at sign-in (IAM policies, an SSO permission set, an app's configuration): where they are managed instead.

url.description: The vendor console page where they are managed (https).

lastChange.description: The latest change of grantedScopes the device saw, and whether Foundry made it.

reason.description: Adapter code only; never raw provider output or credentials.

ConnectorField.description: ConnectorField is one field a sign-in method asks for, rendered by the Web; its value reaches the device's adapter as SignInOptions[ID].

id.description: 1–32 letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter.

pattern.description: A regular expression the whole value must match (checked by the host).

showWhen.description: Shown only while another field of the method holds one of these values.

ConnectorOption.description: ConnectorOption is one choice of a select field.

ConnectorShowWhen.description: ConnectorShowWhen shows a field only while another holds one of Equals.

ConnectorSignInMethod.description: ConnectorSignInMethod is a way to sign in: "guided" (Foundry runs the tool's sign-in on the device and relays the challenge) or "terminal" (the person runs Commands there; Foundry only checks).

commands.description: terminal: what to run there, the first being the usual one.

scopesGroup.description: guided: the authorization group whose scopes the person chooses before signing in; the choice reaches the adapter as signInOptions.scopes (comma-separated).

ConnectorSignIn.description: ConnectorSignIn lists a connector's sign-in methods.

signOut.description: `signOut` false: the tool is signed out in its own terminal, not from the page (absent: Foundry may sign it out).

repeat.description: Signing in again adds another login rather than replacing it (another Limen profile); a signed-in device offers it under this label.

ConnectorSignInRepeat.description: The label of the offer to sign in again.

ConnectorProvides.description: ConnectorProvides is what a connector gives: a tool sessions run, model access for the device (an external model connection).

ConnectorModelRuntime.description: A runtime a model-access connector can serve.

ConnectorModelAccess.description: ConnectorModelAccess names the runtimes a model-access connector serves.

ConnectorExtensionSource.description: ConnectorExtensionSource names the extension a connector comes from.

source.description: Where its files come from, so other devices can install it too.

commit.description: The commit this device installed, when installed from source.

latestCommit.description: The commit source.ref is at now, when the device last looked.

ConnectorExtensionRepository.description: A folder of a git repository holding an extension (docs/connector-extensions.md). The device fetches it with its own git credentials (SSH keys, credential helpers such as GitHub CLI's).

git.description: https://… or an ssh / scp-style remote.

path.description: The folder with foundry-extension.json; the repository's root when empty.

ref.description: A branch or tag; the default branch when empty.

ConnectorSetup.description: ConnectorSetup is how to set an extension connector up on another device.

ConnectorDescriptor.description: ConnectorDescriptor is one connector, as data: a built-in one in internal/connectors/catalog.json, an extension's as its device reports it.

description.description: One sentence: what sessions can do with it.

adapter.description: The adapter that handles this connector's quirks: a built-in one's name, or "extension:<id>" for one an installed extension provides.

signIn.description: How a person signs in; none: Foundry offers no sign-in on the page.

extension.description: Set for a connector an extension on the device provides.

expiryReminderDays.description: A device-held login this close to its expiry is "expiring".

isolationEnv.description: How a session that may not use the device's login is kept from it, with the tool's documented configuration: these variables are set for it.

DeviceConnectorStatus.description: Where a device-held connector stands on one device.

DeviceConnectorState.description: DeviceConnectorState is a device-held connector on one device as last read there. It never holds a credential.

statusDetail.description: Why it is unavailable or failed (a requirement's label, an error).

installSource.description: "foundry": installed by Foundry's managed tools; "device": the device's own.

latestVersion.description: The newest version the device's package source offers, when known.

expiringSince.description: When a check first found the login inside the reminder window.

sessionCheck.description: `sessionCheck` is what checking the connector in the environments a session gets found (see DeviceConnectorSessionCheck). Absent while the login is not read or before the first check.

DeviceConnectorSessionCheck.description: DeviceConnectorSessionCheck separates `signed in` from `usable in a session`. The worker builds the environment a session that may use the login gets, and the one a session that may not gets, from the same code that starts sessions, and checks in them: the tool is found, the login reads as signed in and what the connector promises works (GitHub: git gets github.com credentials) in the first; nothing yields a credential in the second. It never holds a credential.

usable.description: The connector works in the environment of a session that may use it.

reason.description: Why it does not (the tool's or the check's own words, no credential).

isolationHolds.description: A session that may not use the login gets none of it. Absent when the connector has nothing to isolate or the check could not run.

isolationReason.description: What still yielded a credential, when isolation does not hold.

DeviceConnectorUse.description: DeviceConnectorUse rides run_session: what the session may do with a device-held connector on its device ("device_login" or "none").

state.description: `state` is checked metadata only, including separate authorization groups.

ExternalAccountMaterial.description: ExternalAccountMaterial is what a worker needs to let one tool act as an account for one session: the identity, the tool's profile and the gateway handles that stand in for the app secret and the access token. No secret and no real token ever rides it: the tool reaches the provider through the server's gateway (internal/feishugateway), which swaps the handles for the real credentials. It rides run_session and is written into a tool profile the worker removes when the session ends.

tool.description: `tool` is the program the material is for (feishu-cli); ProfileName the profile the worker writes and selects for the session.

gateway.description: `gateway` is how the tool reaches the provider through Foundry.

expiresAt.description: `expiresAt` bounds the handles for the tool's own expiry checks; the server stops honouring them as soon as the session ends.

providerAccountId.description: `providerAccountId` is the provider's own account id that the tool is told natively (Cloudflare: CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, so `cf` finds a zone by domain without listing accounts). Set only when everything the account is bound to belongs to that one account; it is not a secret.

ExternalAccountGateway.description: ExternalAccountGateway is a session's way through the server's gateway for one account: the server path the device's loopback forwarder sends the tool's requests under, and the opaque handles the tool holds in place of the app secret, the user access token and the user refresh token. A handle is useless without the device's credential and dies with the session.

path.description: Server path the device's loopback forwarder sends requests under.

appHandle.description: Stands in for the app secret.

userHandle.description: Stands in for the user access token.

refreshHandle.description: Stands in for the user refresh token; the gateway answers its refresh.

DeviceAccountShare.description: DeviceAccountShare is another person's device under the same system account of the same computer (DeviceProjection.SharesSystemAccountWith).

ownerName.description: The other device's owner, by display name.

acceptedAt.description: `acceptedAt` is when, pairing the later device, someone chose to share; empty when Foundry found the shared account later.

acceptedBy.description: Who chose to share, by display name.

noticePending.description: `noticePending`: the device was there first and its owner has not dismissed the notice that someone else now shares its account.

DeviceAccountIdentity.description: DeviceAccountIdentity is what a worker reports about where it runs, as hashes only: the system account (machine id, account id and the account's own Foundry folder) and the machine.

owned.description: `owned` reports whether the caller owns (and may manage) the device.

managedRoots.description: `managedRoots` are the folders, resolved, the Personal Agent may create projects in, reported by its worker.

outsideFilesOff.description: `outsideFilesOff`: its owner turned off opening its files outside workspaces from chats; set for the owner only (device_files.go).

capabilities.description: `capabilities` are the protocol features its worker declared at its last registration.

connectors.description: `connectors` are what extensions installed on the device provide, as its worker reports them (docs/connector-extensions.md); shown to its owner only.

worker.description: `worker` is the build the device's worker runs and the command that updates it there, reported at registration (0.5.7 and later).

system.description: `system` describes the machine, reported at registration (0.5.7 and later).

workerUpdate.description: `workerUpdate` is set while an update requested from Foundry runs; the server adds it to projections, the worker never reports it.

runner.description: `runner` is the worker's session runner as its connection service last reported it while connected; the server adds it to projections.

lastDisconnect.description: `lastDisconnect` is the last time the device dropped; the server adds it to projections.

lastSeenAt.description: `lastSeenAt` is when the server last recorded the device; for an offline one, when it went offline. ListDevices adds it from the row.

skillsVersion.description: `skillsVersion` changes when the device's scanned skills or the catalog they are compared with change. Workspace data leaves the skill lists out (hundreds of skills per device); clients load one device's list from /api/device-skills and reload it when this changes. The server adds it to projections.

sharesSystemAccountWith.description: `sharesSystemAccountWith` are other people's devices under the same system account of this computer; the server adds it for the device's owner only (device_sharing.go).

DeviceRunner.description: DeviceRunner is a worker's session runner (execution host): its version and whether it waits to switch to the connection service's newer one. State is current, pending, switching or failed (protocol DeviceRunner).

version.description: The runner's own version; absent when it could not be read.

targetVersion.description: The version it switches to: the connection service's.

state.description: unavailable: it does not answer; the connection service reclaims it.

pendingSince.description: Since when it waits to switch (pending).

deadline.description: Until when new turns wait for the new runner (pending).

runningTurns.description: Turns the old runner is running now.

heldTurns.description: New turns waiting for the new runner.

backgroundSessions.description: Sessions with background tasks in the old runner.

waitingFor.description: Pending past the deadline, or with only background work left: new turns go to the old runner, which switches when nothing runs there.

reclaiming.description: A runner that stopped answering is being replaced.

DeviceRunnerTurn.description: DeviceRunnerTurn is a turn a "switch now" stops, as its owner reviews it.

title.description: The session's title, added by the server.

background.description: Only background tasks run for this session; no turn.

DeviceRunnerDetail.description: DeviceRunnerDetail is the runner with the turns it runs now.

WorkerUpdateFailureCode.description:
`exited`: the update command failed. `vanished`: it ended without
reporting. `not_back`: the worker did not reconnect after restarting.

DeviceWorkerUpdate.description: DeviceWorkerUpdate is an update in progress: when it was asked for and the version it brings.

fromVersion.description: `fromVersion` is the version the device ran when the update started.

log.description: `log` is the file on the device the update writes to.

stalled.description: `stalled`: the device still runs FromVersion well after the update started; it did not finish and may be started again.

step.description: `step` is what the update is doing, from the server's status probes: starting, checking, downloading, installing or restarting. After a failure it is the last step seen.

stepDetail.description: `stepDetail` is what the step waits on, such as a retry.

failure.description: `failure` says why the update failed; it may be started again.

failureCode.description: `failureCode`: "exited" (the update command failed), "vanished" (it ended without reporting) or "not_back" (the worker did not reconnect after restarting).

exitCode.description: `exitCode` is the failed update command's exit status.

logTail.description: `logTail` is the end of the update's log on the device, redacted.

DeviceSystem.description: DeviceSystem describes the machine, as its worker reports it.

user.description: The account the worker runs as.

swapBytes.description: Swap space; absent where it is not a fixed size (macOS) or unreadable.

service.description: `service` is how the worker is kept running there (DEV-088).

DeviceServiceState.description: DeviceServiceState is the login service that keeps a worker running, as the worker reads it without administrator rights.

unit.description: The systemd unit or launchd label the worker installed.

linger.description: systemd: whether the account's services keep running after it logs out (`loginctl` Linger). Absent when it could not be read.

logDir.description: Where the worker writes its logs, as typed there (`~/.foundry/logs`).

oomKills.description: The worker's own processes the kernel stopped for lack of memory in the last 7 days, as far as this account can read (its user journal, else its service's memory counters).

DeviceOOMKills.description: DeviceOOMKills counts the worker's processes stopped for lack of memory.

command.description: The command that checks and updates the worker on that machine, as typed there (`~/.foundry/bin/foundry-worker`); absent for a worker run from a source checkout, which updates with git.

maxConcurrentTasks.description: `maxConcurrentTasks` is the turns the device runs at once. An owner saving 0 withdraws their choice: the worker uses its hardware default.

maxConcurrentTasksSource.description: `maxConcurrentTasksSource` is "owner" or "hardware"; workers before DEV-084 leave it out.

hardwareMaxConcurrentTasks.description: What this device's hardware allows by default.

hardware.description: The memory and CPUs that default is computed from.

DeviceHardware.description: DeviceHardware is what a worker's default turn limit is computed from.

capabilities.description: `capabilities` name the protocol features this worker implements. Most are always declared; the server checks only those a worker withholds while it cannot run them (verification_sessions without its sandbox, and those an older execution host still running lacks).

activeSessionIds.description: `activeSessionIds` are execution claims owned by this daemon process; an empty list means it owns no sessions.

servedWorkspaceIds.description: `servedWorkspaceIds`, sent with hello, is every workspace the worker serves; its other workspaces on the server are marked unavailable on the device.

missingWorkspaceIds.description: `missingWorkspaceIds`, sent with hello, are the workspaces the worker still has whose folder is gone; they are marked WorkspaceFolderMissing.

workspace.description: The workspace and, with it, its providerHealth, assets, agents and workspaceFiles are left out when their section is (omittedSections).

stalls.description: `stalls` are stretches the worker's event loop was blocked since its previous registration; the server logs them.

connections.description: `connections` are the worker's own accounts of its previous connections; the server logs them and keeps the latest for the device page.

sections.description: `sections` are the digests of the registration's sections, by name ("device": its agent profiles and provider health; "workspace": the workspace's assets, agents, files, chats and skills), and OmittedSections the ones left out because the server keeps them (see httpapi registration_sections.go).

identity.description: `identity` is the system account and machine the worker runs on, as hashes (device_sharing.go); workers before it report none.

WorkerConnectionReport.description: WorkerConnectionReport is one connection to the server as the worker saw it: who ended it and how long the server had been silent.

durationMs.description: How long the connection lasted, in milliseconds.

closedBy.description: Who ended it: "worker" when the worker gave up (nothing from the server for too long), "server" when a close frame arrived, "network" when the socket ended without one.

error.description: The socket error, e.g. "ECONNRESET: read ECONNRESET".

sinceServerDataMs.description: Milliseconds between the last frame from the server and the close.

sinceServerPingMs.description: Milliseconds between the server's last ping and the close.

proxy.description: Proxy host from the environment, if one is set (not used by the socket).

maxLagMs.description: Worst event-loop delay during the connection, in milliseconds.

sentAfterOpen.description: `sentAfterOpen` is what the worker sent in the first minutes after the connection opened, by message type, largest first.

replayed.description: `replayed` are session outbox messages carried over from an earlier connection.

outboxPeak.description: `outboxPeak` is the most the session outbox and the socket held.

longestSendStallMs.description: `longestSendStallMs` is the longest the socket held bytes the network took none of.

WorkerSentAfterOpen.description: WorkerSentAfterOpen counts a connection's first messages by type.

WorkerSentCount.description: WorkerSentCount is how many messages (of Type) went and their bytes.

WorkerOutboxPeak.description: WorkerOutboxPeak is the fullest a worker's outbox and socket got.

DiagnosticStatus.description: How a diagnostic check came out; "info" only reports a fact.

DiagnosticValue.description: A value a diagnostic check or repair reports.

DiagnosticCheck.description: DiagnosticCheck is one check a worker ran on itself; the web words it by id. Status is ok, info, warn or error.

DeviceDiagnostics.description: DeviceDiagnostics is a worker's report on itself.

connections.description: The worker's last connections to the server, oldest first.

logTail.description: The end of the worker's own logs, secrets removed.

DeviceRepairAction.description: A repair a person can ask a worker to make on itself.

DeviceRepairResult.description: DeviceRepairResult is what a repair the person asked for changed.

values.description: What changed, e.g. the forgotten folders.

DeviceDisconnect.description: DeviceDisconnect is the last time a device dropped, from both ends.

serverReason.description: Why the server ended or lost the connection.

worker.description: The worker's own account, once it reconnected and reported it.

WorkerStall.description: WorkerStall is a stretch when a worker's event loop was blocked.

lagMs.description: How long the loop was blocked, in milliseconds.

activities.description: The worker's long-running activities active during the stall.

EvidenceRequirementSource.description: The Foundry collector that produces an evidence requirement's material, and so the carriers the requirement can receive (EvidenceRequirementSourceCarriers): acceptedCarriers must include one of them. checker_command: stdout and stderr of the criterion's command or project_command checker. checker_http: the exchange of its http checker. candidate_file: a file exported from the sealed candidate. candidate_changes: the Git change list of the sealed candidate against its frozen baselines, i.e. which files were added, modified or deleted. human_upload: a material a person uploads and attests, only for a system_or_human_attested requirement. The checker sources serve deterministic criteria, the others agent criteria. An agent criterion's requirements must name their source before the contract can be confirmed; a deterministic criterion's material comes from its checker whether or not the source is named.

EvidenceRequirementSourceCarriers.description: The carriers each evidence requirement source produces: the one table that contract validation, evidence exports and the clarification read.

CheckConfigurationProjectCommand.description: A command the project already owns, run by Foundry on the sealed candidate. The exit code decides the verdict and the captured output becomes the evidence, so no checker bundle or assertion format exists.

ExitRuleResult.description: One numbered exit rule of a review: every rule must hold before Accept. The rule set is versioned; a review records the version it was judged by.

blockerCodes.description: The blockers that keep the rule from holding.

exitRules.description: Absent on reviews made before exit rules were recorded.

Run.description: Run is where an Issue's current execution stands. The execution is the Issue's issue_execution session, whose id the Run carries; its events and conversation are the session's.

via.description: `via` names where a person's message came from when not the web, such as "feishu".

IssueClarification.description: IssueClarification is the Issue's clarification session and the state of the person's latest message to it.

status.description: `status` is "replying" while the Agent answers the latest message, "failed" when it could not, and "answered" once its reply is recorded.

inputId.description: `inputId` is the session input carrying the latest message.

messageId.description: `messageId` is the person's latest message in the Issue conversation.

revision.description: `revision` and ContentDigest name the draft the message was about; a proposal in the reply revises exactly that draft.

proposalProblems.description: `proposalProblems` are why the proposal in the reply to this message could not be confirmed and was not saved.

earlierProposalProblems.description: `earlierProposalProblems` are the previous message's proposalProblems; this message's turn carries them to the Agent.

ClarificationResponse.description: ClarificationResponse is the clarification session's reply to one message.

ClarificationTurn.description: ClarificationTurn travels with a clarification input: the draft the message is about and the conversation before it, for a session that has lost its native context.

messages.description: The conversation before this message, for a session without native context.

unsavedProposalProblems.description: `unsavedProposalProblems` are why the Agent's previous proposal was not saved, so it can correct the draft.

IssueQuestion.description: IssueQuestion is what an Issue's execution asked the person: something only they can decide (input) or allow (permission). The Issue is blocked on it once the execution's turn ends, and resumes in the same candidate with the answer.

options.description: `options` are choices the Agent offers; the person may answer otherwise.

runId.description: `runId` is the execution session that asked.

createdByUserId.description: `createdByUserId` is the account that started it; agent-created sessions inherit their parent's. Set by the server, never by clients.

executionContract.description: Dispatch-only confirmed content; never authored by the execution Agent.

KnowledgeDocument.description: KnowledgeDocument is an on-device source revision. The control database keeps its hash and provenance; its body is only in transit during file RPC.

documents.description: List entries contain metadata and an empty body; use read for source text.

NativeRuntimeId.description: A runtime Foundry runs natively: Claude Code or Codex.

NativeAccountHold.description: NativeAccountHold is Foundry's durable block, not an online health claim.

SecretPlacement.description:
Where the credential for a profile lives. `local` means the daemon's own
configuration on that machine; `server` means the control plane's sealed
secret store and the key is dispatched per run.

accountLabel.description: Which account the native CLI is signed in as, for telling several logins apart. Identity only — never a token.

cli.description: The device's own Claude Code / Codex program, which Foundry runs.

officialSkills.description: `officialSkills` are the skills this agent ships itself; sessions on it always have them, besides their workspace's selection.

OfficialSkill.description: OfficialSkill is a skill Claude Code or Codex ships itself.

AgentRuntimeUpdate.description: NativeCli is the device's own Claude Code / Codex program, which Foundry runs instead of shipping a copy.

NativeCliInstallResult.description: NativeCliInstallResult is what running the official installer for a device's program produced.

NativeSignInAction.description: NativeSignInAction is one step of a device's official CLI sign-in (native_sign_in): begin starts `claude auth login --claudeai` or `codex login --device-auth` on the device, poll reads it, input hands it the code the person pasted, dismiss ends it, sign_out runs the CLI's own logout.

NativeSignInStep.description: NativeSignInStep is where a device's official sign-in stands. The sign-in runs on the device (its egress, its CLI's token exchange); the server only relays the page to open, a one-time code to enter there, or that the page will show a code to paste back (`codeEntry`). `error` is the CLI's own words, never its page state or a code.

operationId.description: The sign-in this step belongs to; one per runtime on a device.

NativeSignInRequestPayload.description: NativeSignInRequestPayload is native_sign_in (server to worker), answered by native_sign_in_reply.

input.description: The code the person pasted (action input).

NativeSignInReplyPayload.description: NativeSignInReplyPayload is native_sign_in_reply (worker to server). After a sign-in completes or a sign-out, `registration` is the device's fresh report, so its local login shows at once.

NativeSignInInput.description: NativeSignInInput is the body of POST /api/devices/{deviceId}/accounts/{runtime}/sign-in and its /poll, /code and /dismiss, the same as a device connector's sign-in: `requestId` (begin; the same id returns the same running sign-in), `operationId` (the others), and for /code the code the sign-in page showed.

quotaMayBeCached.description: The native interface can return a cached observation without its original timestamp.

runtimeGeneration.description: Native login/config generation; a response for another identity is never reusable.

usedPercent.description: Percentage USED, never remaining. Missing means unknown, not zero.

message.description: Why the check failed, in the agent's words.

reason.description: What kind of failure it was, when known. quota_exhausted means the provider answered that its usage limit is reached; message keeps its words, including when it resets.

CodexApprovalPolicy.description: Codex's approval policy (app-server AskForApproval). Codex 0.167 no longer accepts on-failure; a profile or session that still holds it runs as on-request.

ProfileOrigin.description:
`device` profiles are discovered by a daemon on one machine and cannot move.
`server` profiles are control-plane records usable on any device they are
enabled for.

accountLabel.description: The account a local login is signed in as, when the CLI recorded one.

configSection.description: Where in that file it is defined, e.g. `model_providers.aiden`.

check.description: For a provider found in the device's agent configuration: whether a turn through its agent's SDK answered. It is offered only once that passed.

keySource.description: The key this provider's own configuration names, by name only: a Codex `env_key` such as `$LLM_GATEWAY_KEY`, or `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in a Claude settings file. Absent when it sends no key, or authenticates with a login or a command, neither of which can be copied.

externalSetup.description: `externalSetup` is how an external connection's gateway sets it up on another device (external_connection_setup.go).

connector.description: `connector` names the connector extension whose login gives this external connection (protocol AgentProfileProjection.connector).

models.description: Models offered for this profile wherever a run is configured.

promotedProfileId.description: Set on a device profile whose endpoint already exists as a server profile. The device row stays visible — the machine really is configured this way — but it cannot be promoted twice.

ExternalConnectionSignIn.description: How the installer signs the person in to the gateway.

ExternalConnectionSetupInfo.description: ExternalConnectionSetupInfo is what a gateway registered with `foundry-worker connection add --setup-command …`: one shell line the device's own account runs, never a secret.

command.description: One shell line the device's own account runs; never a secret.

url.description: The gateway's https page about it, if any.

registeredAt.description: `registeredAt` is when the device's worker recorded this command.

CodexTransportMode.description:
The person's choice for a compatible Codex endpoint: `auto` follows what
Codex's own sessions showed about the endpoint, the others are fixed.

ProfileDefinition.description: ProfileDefinition is a control-plane owned profile. It carries no DeviceID and no status: reachability belongs to the device that runs it.

models.description: The models this profile offers. `model` is the default; everything here is selectable in chat and issue runs. Native discovery fills it where a CLI can enumerate, and anything the user adds stays.

contextWindows.description: `contextWindows` is the person's own context window per model id, in tokens. A model without one runs with the window its endpoint reports, else the official model's, else 1M (decided by the worker).

codexTransport.description: `codexTransport` is set on every compatible Codex endpoint (auto, websocket or https): its presence tells the worker this server learns the transport. CodexTransportLearned is the current observation.

codexTransportLearned.description: The current observation for this endpoint (its base URL, at most codexTransportObservationDays old). The override wins over it.

hasCredential.description: True when a credential is sealed in the server secret store. Never the key.

ownerUserId.description: Account that owns this connection; empty only before an admin exists.

promotedFrom.description: `promotedFrom` is set when the profile was promoted from a provider in a device's own configuration.

CodexTransport.description: How Codex reaches a compatible endpoint's Responses API.

CodexTransportObservation.description: CodexTransportObservation is what a Codex session showed about its endpoint's Responses WebSocket: it fell back to HTTPS (Detail is Codex's reason), or a turn completed with the WebSocket on and no fallback.

CodexTransportReport.description: CodexTransportReport is a session's observation, for the profile and base URL it ran (session event metadata codexTransport).

ProfilePromotionSource.description: ProfilePromotionSource is the device provider a server profile was promoted from. Promoting the same provider again updates that profile.

profileId.description: The provider's id on that device, e.g. `codex_provider_gateway`.

deviceBound.description: `deviceBound`: the base URL is the device's own loopback address, which no other device can reach, so the profile may run only on that device.

contextWindow.description: `contextWindow` is the window the endpoint's own catalog reports.

ProfileConnector.description: ProfileConnector is the connector a device model provider comes from.

AgentBackgroundTask.description: AgentBackgroundTask is work a session's agent left running in the background (Claude only). Session events never carry its command line; members read it, redacted, with the task's output.

command.description: Redacted command line, only in members' output reads.

status.description: "ended": it is gone, and the agent did not say how it ended.

stopReason.description: "user": stopped from Foundry; "agent_exit": its agent process ended.

timeLimitMs.description: The deadline the agent gave it (monitors), when it has one.

ownerSubagentTaskId.description: The background subagent that started it.

summary.description: The agent's redacted one-line summary of how it ended.

hasOutput.description: Whether the task writes an output log the device can show.

AgentBackgroundTaskOutput.description: AgentBackgroundTaskOutput is the end of a background task's output as its device read it: plain text, secrets redacted.

command.description: Redacted command line, when the task ran one.

content.description: Plain text: ANSI escapes stripped, secrets redacted.

truncated.description: True when earlier output was left out.

kind.description: "missing": no output was written, or it was cleaned up.

from.description: `from` is set when Content continues an earlier read: what the log gained from that read's LineEnd on.

lineEnd.description: `lineEnd` is where a later read continues; Stable is how many characters of Content cover the log before it (the rest is an unfinished line).

stable.description: How many characters of `content` cover the log before `lineEnd`; the rest is a line still being written, which the next read sends again.

following.description: `following`: the device tells when this running task's log grows.

AgentContextUsage.description: AgentContextUsage is the session's context as its runtime reports it: InputTokens is the whole input of the latest main-agent model request, cache reads and writes included.

inputTokens.description: Absent when unknown, e.g. after a compaction that reports no size.

contextWindow.description: The model's context window, once the runtime has reported it.

model.description: The model that served the request.

compaction.description: Present when the runtime compacted the context.

configuredWindow.description: `configuredWindow` is the window Foundry set for a compatible endpoint's model and where it came from; the runtime may report another.

ContextWindowSource.description: Where a profile's model window comes from, in precedence order.

ConfiguredContextWindow.description: ConfiguredContextWindow is a window Foundry set: the person's setting, the endpoint catalog, the official model, or the 1M default.

AgentContextCompaction.description: AgentContextCompaction marks the runtime compacting the context.

preTokens.description: Tokens in the context before it was compacted.

postTokens.description: `postTokens` and Summary, when the runtime gives them (DEV-083): what is left of the context and the summary the agent continues from.

summary.description: The summary the runtime continues from, when it is readable.

SubagentUsage.description: SubagentUsage is a subagent's own work as Claude reports it: one token total, without an input/output split.

AgentTurnUsage.description: What one turn cost, as the agent's SDK reported it. Token counts share one meaning across providers: `inputTokens` is every prompt token the model read, and cache reads/writes are parts of it, not additions to it.

durationMs.description: Wall time from the runtime taking the turn to its final result.

outputTokens.description: Includes `reasoningTokens` when the provider reports them.

modelRequests.description: Model requests in the turn (Claude reports them; Codex does not).

costUsd.description: `costUsd` is what Claude priced the turn at (list price), when known.

requestUsage.description: `requestUsage` is the tokens of the subagent's model request behind it.

SessionFileDiffAvailability.description:
text: both sides are text a diff can show. binary / tooLarge: one side is
not. noBaseline: no copy from before the session's writes was kept.

SessionFileRecord.description: SessionFileRecord is a file a session's own write tools changed, or its answer named, recorded once per turn by the worker.

workspacePath.description: Relative to the workspace, when the file is inside it.

origin.description: "tool": a write tool changed it; "reference": only the answer names it.

inGitRepo.description: Inside a Git work tree: listed under Changes, otherwise under Files.

inputId.description: The input whose turn recorded it.

agent.description: "main", or the id of the subagent whose tool wrote it.

added.description: Lines this turn's writes added and removed, once the turn ended.

totalAdded.description: Lines added and removed since the session first wrote it.

diff.description: `diff` and TotalDiff say whether the turn's and the session's writes have a text diff: "text", "binary", "tooLarge" or "noBaseline".

totalDiff.description: The same for everything the session wrote to it.

SessionFileReference.description: SessionFileReference is a path an answer names that its device verified.

text.description: As it appears in the answer: a code span's content or a link target.

pending.description: `pending`: no file was there when the answer ended; it links once one is.

SessionFileRead.description: SessionFileRead is one of a session's recorded files, read from its device.

insideWorkspace.description: The file resolves inside the session's workspace.

kind.description: text: `content`; image: `dataBase64` and `mimeType`; binary: size only.

changedSinceRecorded.description: Modified on the device after the turn that recorded it.

SessionFileDiff.description: SessionFileDiff is what a session's own writes changed in one of its recorded files, read from its device: one turn's or the whole session's.

inputId.description: One turn's diff; absent: the whole session's.

before.description: Absent when the diff is unavailable, binary or too large.

beforeLabel.description: empty: the session created it; beforeEdits / turnStart: see `source`.

afterLabel.description: afterEdits: after the session's last write; deleted: it removed it.

mayIncludeOtherEdits.description: Something else also wrote the file while the session edited it.

changedSince.description: The file changed on the device after the session's last write.

unavailable.description: noBaseline: no copy from before the session's edits was kept.

added.description: Lines added and removed, when both sides are text.

SessionToolFrameSource.description: Where a tool frame came from (DEV-075).

SessionToolFrame.description: SessionToolFrame is a screenshot a tool call produced, which the worker keeps as a session file under the workspace's .foundry/attachments/frames (DEV-075). Events carry only this reference; the image is read on demand through the session, by those who may read the session.

callId.description: The tool call whose result carried it.

tool.description: The tool's name as the agent called it.

path.description: Absolute on the device, under the workspace's .foundry/attachments/frames.

inputId.description: The input whose turn recorded it.

AgentScheduledTask.description:
A timer/scheduled task an agent created inside its own session.
 Claude exposes session-scoped cron jobs (CronCreate/ScheduleWakeup). Claude Code fires them while its process runs and brings CronCreate jobs back when the session resumes; the device delivers a timer that comes due while no process holds the session (a ScheduleWakeup always), once, as the session's next input. Codex headless sessions have no equivalent, so timers never appear for Codex threads.

schedule.description: Raw 5-field cron expression in local time.

recurring.description: false for one-shot reminders, true for recurring jobs.

prompt.description: Prompt submitted to the agent when the timer fires.

nextFireAt.description: When Claude Code fires it next (ISO 8601), its id's offset included, as of the snapshot; readers recompute it from `schedule` as time passes.

createdBy.description: `createdBy` is the Claude tool that made the timer, when the device saw the call: Claude Code brings a CronCreate job back when it resumes the session, but not a ScheduleWakeup (dynamic /loop) wakeup, which the device delivers itself once it is due and no process holds it.

AgentSessionSchedule.description: AgentSessionSchedule is the timers a session's agent holds (Claude's CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop): they wake it later, so the session is not idle even when its latest input completed (Status still describes that input). Derived from the latest timer snapshot its device reported (SessionScheduleFromSnapshot).

reportedAt.description: `reportedAt` is when the device reported these timers.

AgentSessionScheduledTimer.description: AgentSessionScheduledTimer is a timer of a session's schedule, without its prompt. NextFireAt is as of ReportedAt; readers recompute it from Schedule as time passes.

firstSeenAt.description: `firstSeenAt` is when a snapshot first listed the timer: a recurring one ends ClaudeRecurringTimerMaxAge later.

AgentSessionTimerFire.description: One automatic, timer-driven turn that ran without a Foundry turn open.

id.description: Scheduled task id when the firing task could be correlated.

scheduledFor.description: `scheduledFor` is when the timer was due (ISO 8601), on a fire the device delivered.

catchUp.description: `catchUp` marks a fire the device delivered late: no process held the session when the timer came due (its worker was down), so it fires once now, however many times it was missed.

AgentSessionGoalStatus.description: Codex reports active, paused, blocked, usageLimited, budgetLimited or complete; a Claude /goal is active until its condition is met or it is cleared.

AgentSessionGoal.description: AgentSessionGoal is the goal the session's agent works toward on its own, as its runtime reports it: Codex's thread goal (thread/goal/*) or Claude Code's /goal (its active_goal message).

objective.description: The objective (Codex) or the condition Claude checks before it stops.

tokensUsed.description: Tokens Codex spent on the goal so far.

timeUsedSeconds.description: Time Codex spent on the goal so far.

iterations.description: How often Claude's check found the condition not yet met.

lastReason.description: Why Claude's last check found the condition not yet met.

AgentSessionGoalSnapshot.description: The session's goal at the time of the event (latest wins); without `goal` the goal was cleared or met.

WorkerFailure.description: WorkerFailure is a versioned diagnosis; the server preserves it without guessing causes.

inputId.description: Bind diagnostics to a dispatch, never to an earlier turn of the chat.

taskOutputFile.description: `taskOutputFile` is a Claude background task's own output log. Workers before it sent that path, and every changed workspace file, as outputFile; that key is no longer read, so those guesses stay hidden.

sessionFile.description: A file the session's tools wrote or its answer named, once per turn.

toolFrame.description: `toolFrame` is a screenshot a tool call produced, kept as a session file on the device (DEV-075).

fileReferences.description: Paths the turn's answer names that the device verified (turn end).

timerSnapshot.description: Snapshots replace earlier ones, so an empty one is kept: it says the last timer or task is gone.

backgroundTaskSnapshot.description: The session's background work at the time of the event (latest wins): running tasks and the most recent finished ones.

timerFire.description: Present on events marking an automatic timer-triggered background turn.

goalSnapshot.description: The session's goal changed (set, progressed, paused, cleared or met).

turnUsage.description: Present on the event that ends a turn the provider reported usage for.

subagentUsage.description: `subagentUsage` is what a Claude subagent has used so far, on its progress and completion events.

requestUsage.description: `requestUsage` is a model request's final tokens (Claude), reported when its stream ends; the event itself is not shown.

contextUsage.description: `contextUsage` is how full the session's context is after a main-agent model request or a compaction; the newest counts.

codexTransport.description: `codexTransport` is what a Codex session showed about its compatible endpoint's Responses WebSocket; the server keeps it for the profile.

sentBySessionId.description: `sentBySessionId`, on a message's event (its input, or a message steered into a running turn), is the session that sent it; empty for what the person typed. Viewers resolve its title themselves, as far as they may read that session.

SessionExecutionBudget.description: SessionInput is one message delivered to a session: the unit of dispatch. It is not a session of its own; identity, permissions and lineage belong to the session it was sent to.

at.description: When the server received the input; its transcript events carry it.

timerFire.description: `timerFire` is set when the input is a timer's prompt: its device resumed the session because the timer was due while no agent process ran it. Its transcript event shows the timer firing.

sentBySessionId.description: `sentBySessionId` is the session that sent the input (create_session's first message, send_message); its transcript event names it.

AgentSession.description: AgentSession is one native agent session (a Claude Code or Codex session) for its whole life. Conversation turns stay inside the native agent; the session carries its latest input and the status of handling it.

createdByUserId.description: `createdByUserId` is the account that started it; agent-created sessions inherit their parent's. Set by the server, never by clients.

nativeSessionId.description: `nativeSessionId` is the native session it resumes on the runtime it runs on (its provider on its device); empty starts one there. The store owns every native session a session ran (sqlitestore native_sessions.go); this is that record's projection.

forkNativeSessionId.description: `forkNativeSessionId`, set while a fork has not answered yet, is the native session NativeSessionID starts as a copy of.

source.description: "digest": a Personal Agent digest summary session (read-only).

role.description: `role` is the job the session does for Foundry; empty for a chat. AgentSessionRoleIssueExecution implements an Issue's confirmed contract in its candidate workspace; AgentSessionRoleIssueClarification talks the Issue through with the person, read-only.

parentSessionId.description: `parentSessionId` records orchestration lineage: the agent session that created this one. Empty for human/browser chats. It is a record for display and limits, never a source of permission.

questionsTo.description: `questionsTo`, set by the server on dispatch, is who answers the session's questions and permission prompts: "person", who holds this chat (a prompt waits in the turn for a while); "parent", the session that created it, reached through its inbox (a prompt ends the turn and its answer is the next message; with no live parent it waits in this chat). Absent: nobody, and prompts are denied at once.

issueId.description: `issueId` runs the session inside an existing Issue candidate worktree instead of the workspace root, enabling safe parallel writes.

groupNameTarget.description: `groupNameTarget` marks a source=naming utility session whose response should rename the auto-created orchestration group with this id.

createdGroupId.description: `createdGroupId` is populated on a session that caused a new orchestration group to be created, so the HTTP layer can trigger async naming.

blockedReason.description: Present for the active status "blocked" (rate limit / permission wait).

input.description: `input` is the latest message sent to the session; Status describes it.

skillRefs.description: Server-resolved workspace skill selection for this session. The runtime is forced to expose only these; an empty present list means none.

response.description: `response` is the answer to the latest input.

activityAt.description: `activityAt` is its last conversation activity: the latest input, or the answer that completed it. Chat lists order by it.

scheduled.description: `scheduled` is set while the agent holds timers that will wake the session; the store keeps it from the session's timer snapshots.

SkillBundleTool.description: SkillBundleTool is a program a bundle needs, installable from the repository's GitHub release of the bundle's version.

assets.description: `assets` are the release downloads per platform.

checksumsUrl.description: `checksumsUrl` is the release's checksum list, when it publishes one.

source.description: `source` is where it installs from: "" (a GitHub release download), "npm" (the npm package Package at Version) or "uv" (the Python package Package at Version, through uv).

registry.description: `registry` is where an npm tool installs from: "" the public registry, an https URL that registry, or "device" each device's own npm settings (its npmrc and scoped registries).

setup.description: `setup` is a step the tool needs after installing (e.g. downloading its browser), run only when the person asks.

signIn.description: `signIn` is the command a person runs once in a terminal on each device after installing (e.g. "auth login"); Foundry only shows it.

SkillToolSetup.description: SkillToolSetup runs one of the installed package's commands with fixed arguments.

command.description: `command` is a command the package installs; empty is the tool itself.

description.description: `description` says what it does, e.g. "Downloads Chrome for Testing".

SkillToolAsset.description: SkillToolAsset is one platform's download of a tool.

SkillDependencyStrength.description: One local skill observed by a device scan.

promotedSkillId.description: Set once this exact entry has been promoted to the server catalog.

dependencies.description: Other installed skills this one references, inferred statically.

sourceDigest.description: SHA-256 of the complete source tree used to build this graph node.

PromotedSkill.description: PromotedSkill is a server catalog entry. Content lives in revisions.

usedByWorkspaces.description: `usedByWorkspaces`: the store lists workspace ids; the API answers with the names of the ones the caller can see.

requires.description: `requires` names the programs the latest revision runs.

SessionSkillRef.description: SessionSkillRef is a resolved (skill, revision) pair attached to a dispatched session. Checksum/ByteSize let the worker verify its cache.

sourceDigest.description: `sourceDigest` authenticates the expanded files independently of ZIP encoding.

bundle.description: `bundle` names the bundle the skill came with, so a session can be told about a large bundle as one entry instead of skill by skill.

SessionSkillBundle.description: SessionSkillBundle is the bundle a session skill came with.

SkillFileInfo.description: SkillFileInfo is cached metadata; file contents are loaded on demand.

WorkspaceKind.description: Every workspace is a project except each person's Personal Agent Workspace.

accessRole.description: `accessRole` is the caller's role in the workspace, set per request.

unavailableOnDevice.description: `unavailableOnDevice` is set while its device, connected, does not serve the folder. Its sessions and history stay; adding the folder on the device again clears it.

kind.description: `kind` is WorkspaceKindProject (sent as absent) or WorkspaceKindPersonalAgent.

archivedAt.description: `archivedAt` is set while the workspace is archived: hidden in an "Archived" group, starting no sessions, everything kept.

migration.description: `migration` is the workspace's move to another device (DEV-146) still under way, or the latest completed one whose old copy on the source device was not deleted yet.

WorkspaceMigrationState.description: preflight, copying, verifying, activating, retiring, then complete; canceled and failed end it too. While copying, verifying or activating the workspace is frozen: no new sessions or messages run there.

WorkspaceMigrationSummary.description: WorkspaceMigrationSummary is what the workspace list shows of a move: the one under way, else the latest complete one whose old copy was not deleted, else the latest move when it failed. A canceled move is never shown.

WorkspaceMigrationFolderWarning.description: Something in the folder that does not travel as it is (the source scan's warnings).

WorkspaceMigrationBlocker.description: Work in the workspace that must end before it can move.

WorkspaceMigrationNotCarried.description: A setting of the workspace tied to the source device; it is not moved and has to be set up again on the target device.

WorkspaceMigrationSourcePurge.description: Whether the old copy on the source device was deleted. A delete that kept files changed after the move leaves state none and records lastAttemptAt and keptCount.

lastAttemptAt.description: When a delete last ran that kept changed files.

keptCount.description: How many changed paths that delete kept.

WorkspaceMigration.description: WorkspaceMigration moves a workspace, same id and history, to a folder on another device (docs/devlog/DEV-146-workspace-migration.md).

step.description: The current sub-step, a short machine word: queued, checking, scanning, checking_target, streaming, retrying, copying_changes, verifying_target, rescanning, activating_target, retiring_source, aborting, done.

files.description: Files received on the target so far.

reason.description: Why it failed or what it waits for, in English; "" when nothing to say.

reasonCode.description: Machine code of reason, for the Web to localize: device_offline, worker_outdated, target_path_taken, target_path_unavailable, not_enough_space, workspace_busy, device_refused, transfer_retrying, transfer_failed, verify_mismatch, canceled_by_person. The migration routes answer errors as {code, error}; their codes: invalid_request, same_device, folder_missing, migration_active, device_offline, target_path_taken (start); no_migration (current); not_cancelable (cancel); not_complete, already_purged, device_offline, device_refused, worker_outdated (purge-source).

WorkspaceMigrationPurgePreview.description: What deleting the old copy removes (confirm false: nothing removed yet) and which paths it keeps because they changed after the move.

WorkspaceUnavailability.description: WorkspaceUnavailability says why a workspace cannot run on its device.

WorkspaceNativeSessionsMoved.description: WorkspaceNativeSessionsMoved is what relinking did to make the workspace's native sessions resumable in its new folder.

copied.description: Native sessions now resumable in the new folder (copied there).

alreadyThere.description: Already resumable there (nothing to do, e.g. Codex, keyed by id).

notFound.description: Not found on the device: their chats continue in a new native session that is given the Foundry conversation.

WorkspaceRelinkSuggestion.description: WorkspaceRelinkSuggestion is a folder that looks like a missing workspace's, moved: "same_workspace" or "same_git_remote".

reason.description: "same_workspace": the folder holds this workspace's own Foundry identity (.foundry/workspace.json), so it is the folder, moved or renamed. "same_git_remote": its Git repository has the same origin remote.

revision.description: Device content identity for bounded instruction files.
